correctness.rationale: The claimed edge partition follows by exhausting the only two path-token move types and checking disjoint path membership. Every path has n distinct token-pair vertices and n-1 edges, and its unique base-wrap move closes an n-cycle. Each odd n-cycle forces at least one uncut edge, while parity lifting of a base cycle maximum cut attains the aggregate bound. The 0/odd edge bipartization equivalence is proved for arbitrary finite graphs. No infinite statement depends on enumeration; the checker explicitly verifies cycles for n=3..150 and independent optimal cuts for n=3..7.

value.rationale: The 2026 token-graph maximum-cut literature supplies only the general parity-lift lower bound. The equal-length cycle decomposition proves that it is sharp for a natural nonbipartite infinite family, with a quantitative frustration index and an explicit optimal cut. This is a complete graph-family classification of edge optimization rather than an arbitrary small parameter case; it also exposes a global edge packing structure that is not implied by known packing or independence numbers.
